YOU.t: This 1-handed ASL sign is produced often with eye gaze directed to the indicated person, thing, group, or empty space: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing up. The index finger points toward the indicated particular person, thing, group, or empty space previously established to represent the indicated entity. Hold the hand briefly in this posture. If the referent is a person, the index finger points toward the center of the person's chest (or the center of the figurative chest of an absent person whom the indicated space has been designated to represent). Thus, if the signer's chest is lower or higher than that of the indicated person, the finger points down or up accordingly.

H.t: This 1-handed ASL sign is produced often with eye gaze directed to the indicated person, thing, group, or empty space: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing up. The index finger points toward the indicated particular person, thing, group, or empty space previously established to represent the indicated entity. Hold the hand briefly in this posture. If the referent is a person, the index finger points toward the center of the person's chest (or the center of the figurative chest of an absent person whom the indicated space has been designated to represent). Thus, if the signer's chest is lower or higher than that of the indicated person, the finger points down or up accordingly.

CONFUSED.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, palm up, base of the hand parallel with the midline plane. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands in at least one full horizontal circle in the same direction, keeping them on opposite sides of the circle.

CONFUSE.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, palm up, base of the hand parallel with the midline plane. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands in at least one full horizontal circle in the same direction, keeping them on opposite sides of the circle.

START.t: ( as a verb ) This two-handed ASL sign is produced as follows: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the extended dominant finger or fingers in between those of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand by rotating it to the next posture while holding the nondominant hand still. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the extended dominant finger or fingers in between those of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing up. Optionally repeat the move by twisting the dominant hand back and forth. ( as a noun ) Produced as above, but with the final posture held briefly.

SKIP.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the sternum, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand. Strike the index finger of the dominant hand against the bent middle finger of the nondominant hand while holding the nondominant hand still. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the sternum, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand.

ABSENT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the sternum, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand. Strike the index finger of the dominant hand against the bent middle finger of the nondominant hand while holding the nondominant hand still. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the sternum, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand.

VEHICLE-COLLIDE.t: Two-handed, as follows when used as a verb: Posture the nondominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, extended fingers of the nondominant hand pointing across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, extended fingers of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Move both hands to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "S" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip of the nondominant hand pointing across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape knuckles contacting knuckles of nondominant hand, tip of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). When used as a noun, both its postures are held briefly (a common ASL hold pattern for nouns).

VEHICLE-COLLISION.t: Two-handed, as follows when used as a verb: Posture the nondominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, extended fingers of the nondominant hand pointing across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, extended fingers of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Move both hands to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "S" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip of the nondominant hand pointing across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape knuckles contacting knuckles of nondominant hand, tip of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). When used as a noun, both its postures are held briefly (a common ASL hold pattern for nouns).

CHINESE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the nondominant shoulder, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Move the hand horizonally across the chest to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the dominant shoulder, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Move the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape on the abdomen, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back.

SANDAL.t: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape over the nondominant hand with the dominant index finger in the space between the nondominant index and middle fingers, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand back and forth, ending with the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

SCHEDULE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape with the dominant hand at the radial edge of the nondominant palm (near the thumb and index finger), dominant palm facing down with extended finger(s) pointing forward and across the body toward the nondominant side. Brush the finger tips of the dominant hand in a "plaid" pattern over the nondominant hand, first across the palm from radial (thumb) side to ulnar (little finger) side. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape with the dominant hand at the ulnar edge of the nondominant palm (between the wrist and little finger), dominant palm facing down with extended finger(s) pointing forward and across the body toward the nondominant side. Then rotate the dominant hand so the palm is facing across and toward the body and place the dominant fingers at the base of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing up with extended finger(s) pointing back and across the body toward the nondominant side. Brush the dominant fingers to the tip of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing up with extended finger(s) pointing back and across the body toward the nondominant side.

SIGN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, extended fingers of the nondominant hand pointing across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, extended fingers of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Move both hands in repeating, alternating circles, moving each up, back, down, then forward.

DEAF.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the index finger touching the jaw. Hold the hand still briefly. Move the hand so the index finger touches the dominant side of the chin. Hold the hand still briefly.

AGREE.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the tip of the index finger touching the side of the forehead, palm facing down. Hold the dominant hand still briefly. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in the center of the space in front of the chest, palm facing down, finger pointing forward. At the same time, move the dominant hand so the radial edge of the index finger contacts that of the nondominant hand, palm facing down, finger pointing forward. Hold both hands still briefly.

DISAGREE.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the tip of the index finger touching the side of the forehead, palm facing down. Hold the dominant hand still briefly. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in the center of the space in front of the chest, finger pointing across toward the dominant side. At the same time, move the dominant hand so the tip of the index finger contacts that of the nondominant hand, finger pointing across toward the nondominant side. Hold both hands still briefly. Move both hands apart so they are several inches away from each other. Hold both hands still briefly.

THINK.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing down. Move the hand so the index finger contacts the temple in the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing down. Hold the hand still briefly.

DON'T-MIND.t: This one-handed ASL sign is usually made while twisting the head from side to side (the typical "no" headshake): Posture the hand in the "1" handshape with the finger tip touching the nose. Hold the hand still briefly. Twist the hand forward so the finger points forward and slightly down. Hold the hand still briefly.

INDIFFERENT.t: This one-handed ASL sign is usually made while twisting the head from side to side (the typical "no" headshake): Posture the hand in the "1" handshape with the finger tip touching the nose. Hold the hand still briefly. Twist the hand forward so the finger points forward and slightly down. Hold the hand still briefly.

ME.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the bent variation of the "1" handshape on the sternum, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

I.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the bent variation of the "1" handshape on the sternum, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

BLEEDING.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape with the palm facing back, fingers pointing across the face, tip of the index finger touching the nose. Wiggle the fingers of the dominant hand while moving it toward the ground.

GO.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape near the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Move both hands to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape a comfortable arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest (with the elbow just slightly bent), extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape near the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing forward.

US.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the bent variation of the "1" handshape on the dominant side of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Move the hand in a horizontal arc forward then to the nondominant side. Posture the dominant hand in the bent variation of the "1" handshape on the nondominant side of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Hold the hand still briefly. To indicate that the non-first-person members of the group are literally or figuratively located somewhere, the signer may lean his or her body and shift the contact point toward that location.

THE-THREE-OF-US.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape within a few inches of the chest, in between the signer's chest and the other referents, dominant palm facing up. Move the hand in repeated horizontal circles. The size of the circles indicates the distance the other two referents are from the signer. Hold the hand still briefly.

THE-THREE-OF.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape at least half an arm's length in front of the chest, on the same side of the signer as the referents, dominant palm facing up. Move the hand in repeated horizontal circles. The size of the circles indicates the distance the referents are from each other. Hold the hand still briefly.

LISTEN.t: One-handed, with the head tilted toward to the source of the noise: Posture the dominant hand in the "Bent 3" handshape at the dominant ear (behind the cheek, above the jaw), palm facing forward. Hook the fingers repeatedly to indicate the intensity.

AWKWARD.t: Two-handed, with a facial expression suggesting awkwardness: Posture the nondominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands alternatingly and repeatedly up and down. Posture the nondominant hand in the "3" shape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, dominant palm facing down. ( clumsy ): A different facial expression expresses the meaning "clumsy", typically with the mouthing "TH".

RAINBOW.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "4" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape near the nondominant hand's fingertips, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing down. Move the dominant hand in an arc upward, then across toward the dominant side, then down, to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "4" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up. Hold both hands still briefly.

HOTDOG.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "C" shape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm. Move the dominant hand down so the index finger contacts the palm once or twice. Hold both hands still briefly.

FALL-ASLEEP.t: Two-handed, with the head dropping and eyes closing along with the dominant hand: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing down. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape aside and in front of the nose, dominant palm facing down. Posture the nondominant hand in the "A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

FALL-IN-LOVE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the mouth, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the dominant hand in an arc upward, then forward, then down onto the base of the nondominant palm. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm, ulnar (little-finger-side) edge of the dominant hand down. Bounce the dominant hand up, then forward, then back down to the tip of the nondominant palm. Optionally bounce multiple times along the path from palm base to tip. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the tip of the nondominant palm, ulnar (little-finger-side) edge of the dominant hand down.

CORRECT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended fingers of the nondominant hand pointing forward and across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the radial (thumb) side of the nondominant hand, extended fingers of the dominant hand pointing forward and across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Hold both hands still briefly.

DIFFERENT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant index finger pointing across, forward, and optionally up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant index finger across the nondominant index finger. Move both hands apart to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest.

SAME.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant index finger pointing across, forward, and optionally up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant index finger across the nondominant index finger. Move both hands apart to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest.

ALIKE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant index finger pointing across, forward, and optionally up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant index finger across the nondominant index finger. Move both hands apart to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest.

RED.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Retract the index finger while moving the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape within a few inches from the chin, dominant palm facing back.

DUE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down. Drop the dominant hand down so the finger tip contacts the nondominant hand at least once. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down.

WHERE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Move the finger in a repeated, small side-to-side motion, pivoting at the wrist. When used interrogatively, this sign is produced with furrowed eyebrows, squinted eyes, head tilted, and a very small headshake (i.e. pivoting slightly from side to side, not nearly so much as that of a "no" gesture).

NERVOUS.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the trunk, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down. Shake the dominant finger in a small side-to-side motion.

PHOTOGRAPH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape near the nondominant cheek, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape near the dominant cheek, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Squeeze both index fingers into hooks. Posture the nondominant hand in the "X" handshape near the nondominant cheek. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape near the dominant cheek.

WHEN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape near the nondominant hand's fingertips, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand in one or more horizontal circles around the nondominant hand before bringing it down so the tips of the two index fingers touch. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape touching the tip(s) of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. When used interrogatively, this sign is produced with furrowed eyebrows, squinted eyes, head tilted, and a very small headshake (i.e. pivoting slightly from side to side, not nearly so much as that of a "no" gesture).

TOMATO.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape on the lower lip, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand down so the index finger brushes the radial side of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "O" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a few inches of the radial (thumb) side of the nondominant hand.

MEET.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand several inches from the thumb of the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the dominant hand to the nondominant hand so the backs of the thumbs contact each other. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the thumb of the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. This is a directional sign, so the location and orientation of the hands change for inflection. See Inflection, below, for details.

FOUR-YEARS-OLD.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape at the chin, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the hand in an arc, first down, the forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape several inches from the chin, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up.

WEEK.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Slide the dominant hand across the nondominant hand, toward the tips of the nondominant fingers. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

1-WEEK.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Slide the dominant hand across the nondominant hand, toward the tips of the nondominant fingers. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

MONTH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape touching the tip(s) of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing back. Slide the dominant index finger down the radial edge of the nondominant hand, toward the base of the thumb. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape touching the base of the thumb of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

1-MONTH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape touching the tip(s) of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing back. Slide the dominant index finger down the radial edge of the nondominant hand, toward the base of the thumb. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape touching the base of the thumb of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

TELL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand forward and extend the wrist so the index finger tilts forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape several inches from the chin, dominant palm facing up.

DEVIL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, palm facing forward. Repeatedly flex and release the index finger and middle finger, alternating between the "3" and "bent 3" shapes.

CAN'T.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, with the extended finger pointing to the dominant side. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape above and behind the nondominant hand, palm facing forward. Quickly lower the dominant hand, striking the extended fingers against each other, ending with the dominant hand a short distance below the nondominant hand.

CAN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, with the extended finger pointing to the dominant side. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape above and behind the nondominant hand, palm facing forward. Quickly lower the dominant hand, striking the extended fingers against each other, ending with the dominant hand a short distance below the nondominant hand.

ALONE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the dominant side of the neck, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up and palm facing back. Move the hand in horizontal circles.

SOMEONE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the dominant side of the neck, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up and palm facing back. Move the hand in horizontal circles.

ESCAPE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand forward to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape FromFinger, palm facing forward.

ESTRANGED.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand forward to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape FromFinger, palm facing forward.

THREE.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "3" shape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up.

SAW.t: This two-handed ASL sign has two postures: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape near the body, lateral with the dominant shoulder, at shoulder height, palm facing back, thumb on top. Posture non-dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about an elbow's length out from the center body, chest high, palm facing down, fingers pointing toward the dominant side. Move the dominant hand repeatedly frontward toward the nondominant side and backward toward the dominant side to the next posture while holding the non-dominant hand in this posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape on the back of the nondominant hand, palm facing back, thumb on top.

FINE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape on the sternum, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Touch the thumb one or more times to the sternum. The number of iterations, speed, angle of the hand, and distance moved from the sternum are variable and may be used for emphasis or to add certain frames, styles, or semantic overtones.

COUNT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat 9" shape at the base of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand forward while holding the nondominant hand in this posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat 9" shape with the extended dominant finger or fingers in between those of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Alternatively, both palms may face each other with the extended fingers of each hand pointing up. In this form, the dominant hand moves up instead of forward. Alternatively, the dominant hand may contact the nondominant hand multiple times while it moves from base to tip.

RUDE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand across the nondominant palm toward the dominant side of the body to the following posture while holding the nondominant hand still. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down.

SHARP.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Briefly hold the dominant hand in this posture. Hold the nondominant hand in this posture for the duration of the sign. Flick the dominant hand forward and slightly upward. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand near the back of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

INTERNET.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the nondominant hand facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with tip of the middle finger touching the tip of the other middle finger, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up.. Twist both hands repeatedly in opposite directions, pivoting on the tips of the middle fingers.

MAN.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape with the thumb contacting the forehead. Move the dominant hand down while changing handshape to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape on the chest, thumb of the dominant hand pointing back.

EARTH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "S" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the thumb and middle finger grasping the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Twist the dominant hand repeatedly along the axis running through the tips of the thumb and the index finger. Hold the dominant hand still briefly.

GLOBE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "S" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the thumb and middle finger grasping the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Twist the dominant hand repeatedly along the axis running through the tips of the thumb and the index finger. Hold the dominant hand still briefly.

BREASTS.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape a few inches in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape a few inches in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing back. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

SAD.t: Two-handed, with a sad expression on the face: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape a few inches in front of the nondominant side of the face, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape a few inches in front of the dominant side of the face, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape a few inches in front of the nondominant side of the neck, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape a few inches in front of the dominant side of the neck, dominant palm facing back. Hold both hands briefly in this posture. The degree or type of sadness can be indicated with various nuanced facial expressions and by slowing the downward movement or holding the final posture longer.

SALAD.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing up. Move both hands up and inward to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up.

FRANCE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "9" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the dominant side of the neck, dominant palm facing down. Move the hand aside while twisting the hand to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "9" handshape in front of and beside the neck, dominant palm facing up.

WIKTIONARY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "6" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand in repeating circles, each brushing the nondominant palm back toward the body, then up, then forward, then down.

SCARED.t: This two-handed ASL sign has two postures: Posture both hands in the "5" handshape just in front of the shoulders with palms facing back. Move both hands to the following posture. Posture both hands in the "5" handshape just in front of the chest with palms facing back. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

FEAR.t: This two-handed ASL sign has two postures: Posture both hands in the "5" handshape just in front of the shoulders with palms facing back. Move both hands to the following posture. Posture both hands in the "5" handshape just in front of the chest with palms facing back. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

SNOW.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside from the forehead, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside from the forehead, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands down slowly while wiggling the fingers. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing down. Be sure to move the hands down slowly to differentiate this sign from Claw5@SideForeheadhigh-PalmDown-Claw5@SideForeheadhigh-PalmDown Claw5@SideChinhigh-PalmDown-Claw5@SideChinhigh-PalmDown Claw5@SideChesthigh-PalmDown-Claw5@SideChesthigh-PalmDown ( " rain " ) API.

SHAMPOO.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape at the nondominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Hold both hands still briefly. Move both hands in a circular motion as if you are washing your hair using the shampoo.

FAVORITE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Hold hand still briefly. Tap the middle finger of the dominant hand on the chin two or more times. Hold the hand still briefly.

PREFER.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Hold hand still briefly. Tap the middle finger of the dominant hand on the chin two or more times. Hold the hand still briefly.

MOTHER.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape at the chin, thumb of the dominant hand pointing back. Touch the thumb to the chin one or more times.

I-CONTACT-YOU.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the nondominant hand facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up. Hold both hands still briefly. Tap both middle fingers together two or more times. Hold both hands still briefly.

CONTACT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the nondominant hand facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up. Hold both hands still briefly. Tap both middle fingers together two or more times. Hold both hands still briefly.

TOUCH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the nondominant hand facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up. Hold both hands still briefly. Tap both middle fingers together two or more times. Hold both hands still briefly.

NETWORK.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of the center of the chest, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the nondominant hand facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up. Hold both hands still briefly. Tap both middle fingers together two or more times. Hold both hands still briefly.

SECRET.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape at the mouth with lips closed, thumb back, palm facing across. Touch the hand to the mouth once or more. Hold the hand still briefly.

FAMILY.t: Two-handed: Posture both hands in the "9" handshape in front of the chest, palms facing forward, the thumb and index finger of each hand touching the thumb and index finger of the other hand. Hold both hands still briefly. Move each hand in a horizontal circle while twisting the wrist. Posture both hands in the "9" handshape in front of the chest, palms facing back, the little finger of each hand touching the little finger of the other hand. Hold both hands still briefly.

TAKE-IT-EASY.t: Two-handed, with the lips pushed out and with the head tilted a little to one side: Posture both hands in the "5" handshape, the dominant hand in front of the chest, the nondominant hand to the nondominant side, both palms facing down. Drop both hands down to the height of the trunk. Move both hands up and toward the dominant side. Drop both hands down to the height of the trunk.

ACT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing down. Swing both hands repeatedly from side to side in valley-shaped arcs, each hand moving simultaneously with the other hand toward each side.

ACTION.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing down. Swing both hands repeatedly from side to side in valley-shaped arcs, each hand moving simultaneously with the other hand toward each side.

ACTIVE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing down. Swing both hands repeatedly from side to side in valley-shaped arcs, each hand moving simultaneously with the other hand toward each side.

RAIN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside from the forehead, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside from the forehead, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside of the chin, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside of the chin, dominant palm facing down. Hold both hands still briefly. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, dominant palm facing down. Hold both hands still briefly.

ALBANY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the sternum, palm facing forward. Move the dominant hand to the dominant side and then diagonally downward to the nondominant side in one smooth motion. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the abdomen (above the waist), palm facing forward.

MYSELF.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger on the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing back. Touch the back of the thumb twice against the chest. Hold the hand still briefly.

SELF-ONLY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger on the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing back. Touch the back of the thumb twice against the chest. Hold the hand still briefly.

SELF-ONLY-PL-1.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger on the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing back. Touch the back of the thumb twice against the chest. Hold the hand still briefly.

SELF-ONLY-PL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger on the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing back. Touch the back of the thumb twice against the chest. Hold the hand still briefly.

YOURSELF.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger about half an arm's length in front of the chest. Move the hand in a small front-and back motion, ending with a forward thrust. Hold the hand still briefly.

SELF-ONLY-1.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger about half an arm's length in front of the chest. Move the hand in a small front-and back motion, ending with a forward thrust. Hold the hand still briefly.

OURSELVES.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in a shape similar to the "A" handshape (i.e. with the fingers together and curled into a fist, the thumb unopposed and closed) but with the tip of the thumb extended about an inch past the edge of the index finger on the dominant side of the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the same shape on the nondominant side of the chest, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

THIRTEEN.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open U" (Hu) handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Repeatedly flatten and extend the index and middle fingers, keeping them together. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back.

BEAUTIFUL.t: One-handed, usually with a pleasant smile, often with eyes closed by the end of the sign: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape near the dominant cheek, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand in a circle around the entire face (up the dominant side, across, down, and back to the dominant side), ending with a closing of the fingers into the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape near the dominant jaw, dominant palm facing back. Hold the final posture briefly. The sign may be produced quickly to mention beauty in passing or it may be produced slowly for emphasis. Optionally shake the hand in the final posture for emphasis.

UGLY.t: One-handed, usually with a pleasant smile, often with eyes closed by the end of the sign: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape near the dominant cheek, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand in a circle around the entire face (up the dominant side, across, down, and back to the dominant side), ending with a closing of the fingers into the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape near the dominant jaw, dominant palm facing back. Hold the final posture briefly. The sign may be produced quickly to mention beauty in passing or it may be produced slowly for emphasis. Optionally shake the hand in the final posture for emphasis.

BEAUTY.t: One-handed, usually with a pleasant smile, often with eyes closed by the end of the sign: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape near the dominant cheek, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand in a circle around the entire face (up the dominant side, across, down, and back to the dominant side), ending with a closing of the fingers into the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape near the dominant jaw, dominant palm facing back. Hold the final posture briefly. The sign may be produced quickly to mention beauty in passing or it may be produced slowly for emphasis. Optionally shake the hand in the final posture for emphasis.

VOMIT.t: Two-handed, with head movement and facial expression imitating the act of vomiting: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape within a several inches of the tip of the extended finger on the dominant hand farthest from the thumb. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape at the mouth. Move the hands forward and down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape within a several inches of the tip of the extended finger on the dominant hand farthest from the thumb. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape within several inches from the mouth.

DYE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "9" handshape in front of and beside the neck, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "9" handshape in front of and beside the neck, dominant palm facing down. Move the hands down to the following posture, then back up and back down again. Posture the nondominant hand in the "9" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "9" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, dominant palm facing down.

CHARMED.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape with the dominant hand at the thumb of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Wiggle the fingers of both hands while moving them toward the dominant side. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and to the dominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape with the dominant hand at the thumb of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

DONT-WANT.t: Two-handed, typically with the head shaking "no": Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up. Twist the hands inward then down while opening the fingers in a gesture that suggests throwing something away. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down.

LIKE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape within a few inches from the chest, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand away from the chest while drawing the thumb and middle finger closed. Posture the dominant hand in the "8" handshape several inches from the chest, dominant palm facing back.

COOL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape on the chest. Wiggle the fingers of the dominant hand.

WHAT.t: Two-handed, with a questioning face, usually with furrowed brows: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing up. Move the hands from side to side repeatedly. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, dominant palm facing up.

ANGRY.t: One-handed, with an angry scowl: Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape within a few inches from the nose, dominant palm facing back. Clench the fingers into a tight claw and hold briefly.

PRACTICE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape dominant hand on the radial (thumb) side of the extended finger of the nondominant hand, palm facing across. Move the dominant hand repeatedly from base to tip of the nondominant index finger.

COLOR.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Wiggle the fingers of the dominant hand.

WHITE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Draw the hand forward from the chest while closing it. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape within a few inches from the chest, dominant palm facing back.

DONT-LIKE.t: One-handed, with a "no" headshake or an expression of distaste: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape within a few inches from the chest, dominant palm facing back. Draw the hand forward from the chest while closing the thumb and middle finger. Posture the dominant hand in the "8" handshape several inches from the chest, dominant palm facing back. Twist the hand downward while releasing the middle finger. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape several inches from the chest, dominant palm facing down.

SORRY.t: One-handed, with a concerned expression: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Make a large vertical circle on your chest with your palm facing backward.

SORROW.t: One-handed, with a concerned expression: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Make a large vertical circle on your chest with your palm facing backward.

APOLOGIZE.t: One-handed, with a concerned expression: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Make a large vertical circle on your chest with your palm facing backward.

ATTEMPT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "A" handshape a few inches in front of the nondominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape a few inches in front of the dominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Pronate the hands while moving them forward to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "A" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down.

WATER.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "6" handshape at the chin, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up. After touching the chin, hold the hand still briefly.

SIX.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "6" handshape.

FIVE.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up.

FIMM.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up.

FOX.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "9" handshape at the nose, palm facing forward. Twist twice, pivoting around the nose.

MACAU.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape at the chin, extended fingers of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Twist the hand twice, pivoting on the index finger.

PLEASE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand around the chest, at least one full circle. When used as a noun, the hand is held briefly before and after the circling movement.

PLEASURE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand around the chest, at least one full circle. When used as a noun, the hand is held briefly before and after the circling movement.

HELLO.t: One-handed, with a smile: Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, palm facing forward. Hold the dominant hand briefly in this posture. Move the dominant hand to the following posture. Move head slightly forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside from the forehead, palm facing forward. Hold the dominant hand briefly in this posture.

HOW.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands to the following posture by rotating the finger tips upward and the thumbs away from each other. Posture the nondominant hand in a relaxed version of the "bent B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in a relaxed version of the "bent B" handshape with the dominant hand at the ulnar edge (little-finger side) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing up. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

BUSY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the radial (thumb) side of the nondominant wrist, palm facing forward. Hold the position of both hands briefly. Move the dominant hand side-to-side while holding the position of the nondominant hand. Hold the position of both hands briefly. Note: The number of iterations and speed are variable and may be used for emphasis.

BUSINESS.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the radial (thumb) side of the nondominant wrist, palm facing forward. Hold the position of both hands briefly. Move the dominant hand side-to-side while holding the position of the nondominant hand. Hold the position of both hands briefly. Note: The number of iterations and speed are variable and may be used for emphasis.

ENJOY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the trunk, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand around the chest, through the following posture. Move the nondominant hand around the trunk, through the following posture. Continue moving both hands at least one full circle.

IMPROVE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the tip (wrist end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the base (elbow end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back.

IMPROVED.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the tip (wrist end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the base (elbow end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back.

IMPROVEMENT.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the tip (wrist end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the base (elbow end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing back.

GOOD.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Hold the dominant hand briefly in this posture. Hold the nondominant hand in this posture for the duration of the sign. Move the dominant hand downward to contact the nondominant palm in the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing up.

WELL.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Hold the dominant hand briefly in this posture. Hold the nondominant hand in this posture for the duration of the sign. Move the dominant hand downward to contact the nondominant palm in the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing up.

BEER.t: This one-handed ASL sign has one posture: Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the dominant cheek. The nondominant hand is not used. Move the dominant hand in circles around the cheek.

OPEN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, palm facing forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape with the dominant hand at the thumb of the nondominant hand, palm facing forward. Swing the dominant hand along back to the next posture while holding the nondominant hand still. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, palm facing forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape a few inches in front of the neck, over and just ahead of the shoulder, palm facing across.

DARK.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape several inches to the nondominant side of and about half an arm's length in front of the nose, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape several inches to the dominant side of and about half an arm's length in front of the nose, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands in arcs, first across the face then down, to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, dominant palm facing back.

DARKEN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape several inches to the nondominant side of and about half an arm's length in front of the nose, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape several inches to the dominant side of and about half an arm's length in front of the nose, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands in arcs, first across the face then down, to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the neck, dominant palm facing back.

DRAMA.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, thumb of the dominant hand pointing back. Move both hands through the following posture in alternating circles brushing the chest, then down, forward, and up with each circle.

BOX.t: This ASL sign is produced as follows: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Drop both hands down to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the trunk. Move both hands to the following posture by bending the wrists and extending the dominant arm. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape a few inches in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape almost a full arm's length in front of the center of the chest, dominant palm facing back. Drop both hands down to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape a few inches in front of the center of the trunk, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape almost a full arm's length in front of the center of the trunk, dominant palm facing back.

LIVER.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape just below the right side of the ribcage, where the liver is located. Tap the fingers lightly against the abdomen a couple of times. Note: This is one of the few ASL signs that is always made with the right hand, regardless of which hand is dominant.

SANDWICH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape within a few inches from the mouth, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape cupped over the back of the dominant hand, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands back toward the mouth to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape at the mouth, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape cupped over the back of the dominant hand, dominant palm facing back.

FORGET.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape at the forehead, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand to the following posture while changing the handshape. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape several inches from the dominant side of the forehead, dominant thumb pointing toward the dominant side.

SCHOOL.t: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Clap the hands about two times.

SCIENCE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, thumb of the dominant hand pointing down. Move both hands in repeated alternating circles across (toward the center), down, aside (toward the outside), and up. Hold both hands still briefly.

RELIEVED.t: Two-handed, with rounded, pursed lips, and usually with a puff of air during the downward movement: Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape on the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands down to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape on the abdomen, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing down.

RELIEVE.t: Two-handed, with rounded, pursed lips, and usually with a puff of air during the downward movement: Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape on the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands down to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape on the abdomen, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing down.

RELIEF.t: Two-handed, with rounded, pursed lips, and usually with a puff of air during the downward movement: Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape on the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands down to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape on the abdomen, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing down.

GIVE-IN.t: One-handed, with the lips initially pressed tightly together, then released as the jaw drops in the final posture: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Hold the hand still briefly before moving it forward to the following posture while releasing the lips and dropping the jaw. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape several inches from the chest, dominant palm facing up.

LATE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape beside the trunk, dominant palm facing back. Nod the wrist repeatedly so the hand waves back.

NOT-YET.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape beside the trunk, dominant palm facing back. Nod the wrist repeatedly so the hand waves back.

TOMORROW.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape at the jaw (below the cheek and ear, behind the chin), thumb of the dominant hand pointing back. Move the hand forward while twisting the hand into the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape a couple of inches forward from the cheek, thumb of the dominant hand pointing up.

OUR.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape on the dominant side of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. The radial (thumb) edge of the hand is in contact with the chest. Move the hand in an arc while rotating it so that it faces the opposite direction. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape on the nondominant side of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. The ulnar (little finger) edge of the hand is in contact with the chest. If it is necessary to indicate which people other than the signer are the possessors, the signer may lean to the side near those people.

MY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back.

YOUR.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. The palm faces the literal or figurative location of the referent (the possessor).

YOURS.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. The palm faces the literal or figurative location of the referent (the possessor) farthest to the nondominant side of the signer. Slightly drop the hand and move it in an arc toward the dominant side of the body. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. The palm faces the literal or figurative location of the referent (the possessor) farthest to the dominant side of the signer.

ANYTHING.t: Two-handed: Move both hands from the sides toward the center so the wrists cross each other in the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "A" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape at the nondominant wrist, dominant palm facing up. Move both hands apart toward the sides while opening the fingers and thumb to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing up. Hold both hands still briefly.

DONT-KNOW.t: One-handed, optionally shaking the head "no": Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Twist the hand away from the head in a manner that suggests throwing away.
