Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape several inches from the dominant side of the forehead, dominant palm facing toward the dominant side.

KNOW.t: One-handed, optionally shaking the head "no": Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Twist the hand away from the head in a manner that suggests throwing away. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape several inches from the dominant side of the forehead, dominant palm facing toward the dominant side.

INTRODUCE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, backs of the extended or bent fingers of the nondominant hand facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape within a several inches of the tip of the extended finger on the nondominant hand, backs of the extended or bent fingers of the dominant hand facing down. Move the hands toward each other so the finger tips meet in the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), backs of the extended or bent fingers of the nondominant hand facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape touching the tip(s) of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, backs of the extended or bent fingers of the dominant hand facing down.

WELCOME.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape several inches in front from the trunk (in front of and just below the chest), dominant palm facing up. Move the hand horizontally in to the trunk to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing up.

THANK-YOU.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand forward and down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape several inches from the chin, dominant palm facing up.

REMEMBER.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Move the dominant hand down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing across the body toward the dominant side (contralaterally). Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the thumb of the nondominant hand, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally).

TIRED.t: Two-handed, with the head dropping forward and down along with the hands: Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape on the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape on the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing back. Roll the hands down the chest to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "bent B" handshape on the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape on the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up.

PAGE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, thumb of the dominant hand pointing down. Move the dominant hand in a repeated circle, each moving from the palm to the nondominant side, then up, then back to the dominant side, then down, contacting the nondominant palm each time.

SLOW.t: Two-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Draw the dominant hand back at a medium or slow pace to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the nondominant wrist, dominant palm facing down. Optionally continue moving the dominant hand farther up the nondominant forearm.

BAD.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Rotate the hand forward while moving it forward and aside. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape several inches from the chin, dominant palm facing down.

NICE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Wipe the dominant hand across the nondominant hand from base to the fingers. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the dominant hand at the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

BROWN.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape Cheek, palm facing forward. Slide the hand down the face to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape at the jaw (below the cheek and ear, behind the chin), palm facing forward.

PUSH-ASIDE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the trunk, dominant palm facing toward the dominant side. Move both hands somewhat to the right.

HAPPY.t: Two-handed, with a smile: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing back. Repeatedly brush both hands up and off the chest, returning to the chest after each brush. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of and beside the neck, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of and beside the neck, dominant palm facing back.

WHY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Move the hand away from the head while closing the index, middle, and ring finger. Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape several inches from the dominant side of the forehead. When used interrogatively, the sign is produced with furrowed eyebrows, squinted eyes, head tilted, and a very small headshake (i.e. pivoting slightly from side to side, not nearly so much as that of a "no" gesture). When used in a rhetorical question, the sign is produced with raised eyebrows and the head tilted slightly.

FIFTEEN.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Flatten and extend the four fingers (not including the thumb) at least twice, keeping them together. Posture the dominant hand in a bent version of the "open B" shape, with the four fingers bent at the proximal joint but otherwise extended and together, thumb extended to make a flat hand with a gap between the thumb and the edge of the hand about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back.

GESTURE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest. Move the hands in repeated, alternating circles, each going up, forward, down, then back.

EXCUSE-ME.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the chest, with the fingers pointing forward, palm up. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape touching the base of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Brush the fingertips of the dominant hand across the nondominant hand to the fingertips. Variations may do this action once, repeat it, or continue doing it until the desired effect is attained (i.e. if trying to pass by or through a signer's conversation).

EXCUSE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the chest, with the fingers pointing forward, palm up. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape touching the base of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Brush the fingertips of the dominant hand across the nondominant hand to the fingertips. Variations may do this action once, repeat it, or continue doing it until the desired effect is attained (i.e. if trying to pass by or through a signer's conversation).

ABLE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "A" handshape Sternumhigh, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape Sternumhigh, dominant palm facing down. Move the hands downward firmly a short distance. Variations may double this movement.

NIGHT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "bent B" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Tap the heel of the dominant hand about twice on the back of the nondominant hand.

FLOOR.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "B" handshape in neutral space abutting the center line of the body, with palm facing down and the tips of the fingers facing away from the signer. Posture the dominant hand in the "B" handshape in neutral space abutting the center line of the body and hence the opposite hand, with palm facing down and the tips of the fingers facing away from the signer. Hold both hands still briefly. Move both hands smoothly away from one another until they are approximately as far as apart as the signer's shoulders. Hold both hands still briefly.

WHATS-UP.t: Two-handed, with a questioning face: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape on the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands in arcs from the chest up and out to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of and beside the neck, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape in front of and beside the neck, dominant palm facing back. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

MUCH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of the center of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape touching the tip(s) of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, palm facing across. Move both hands to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, palm facing across. Alternatively, the hands may begin near each other rather than touching. Alternatively, the palm tips may point up rather than forward.

GAY.t: This one-handed ASL sign has one posture: Posture the dominant hand in the "G" handshape with the tips of the index finger and thumb touching the chin, radial edge (the edge of the index finger and thumb) on top. Hold the hand briefly in this posture.

BUTTER.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "H" handshape at the tip of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Hold the nondominant hand in this posture for the entire duration of the sign. Draw the fingers of the dominant hand over the nondominant palm toward its base. Posture the dominant hand in the "H" handshape at the base of the nondominant palm. Move the dominant hand to the starting posture and repeat at least once, typically twice. Hold the hands briefly in the final posture.

PICTURE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, palm facing forward. Move both hands to contact each other in the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, radial (thumb-side) edge of the dominant hand facing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Hold both hands briefly in this position.

QUEEN.t: One-handed: Place the "G" handshape between the nondominant shoulder and the sternum, thumb and index finger pointing down. The nondominant hand is not used. Hold the hand briefly in this posture. Move the hand down and across to the following posture. Place the dominant hand in the "G" handshape on the dominant side of the abdomen, thumb and index finger pointing down. Hold the hand briefly in this posture.

IRONIC.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "corna" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "corna" handshape at the nose. Move both hands in opposite directions past the front of the chest, brushing the dominant hand over the nondominant one as they pass each other. Posture the nondominant hand in the "corna" handshape in front of the center of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "corna" handshape with the arms crossed near the wrists.

IRONY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "corna" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "corna" handshape at the nose. Move both hands in opposite directions past the front of the chest, brushing the dominant hand over the nondominant one as they pass each other. Posture the nondominant hand in the "corna" handshape in front of the center of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "corna" handshape with the arms crossed near the wrists.

DICTIONARY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "D" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand in repeating circles, each brushing the nondominant palm back toward the body, then up, then forward, then down.

TEACH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape within a few inches of the nondominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple. Posture the nondominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape several inches from the nondominant side of the forehead. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape several inches from the dominant side of the forehead. Hold both hands still briefly.

MONEY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, backs of the extended or bent fingers of the dominant hand facing down. Move the dominant hand down so the back of the fingers contact the nondominant palm at least twice.

NAME.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "H" handshape in front of the center of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "H" handshape dominant hand on the radial (thumb) side of the extended finger of the nondominant hand. Move the dominant hand repeatedly up and down so the ulnar side of the second knuckle of the middle finger of the dominant hand contacts the radial side of the second knuckle of the middle finger of the nondominant hand. Hold both hands still briefly.

OUTSIDE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat C" handshape about half an arm's length in front and aside of the mouth, palm facing across. Close the fingers to the thumb, forming the "flat O" shape, reopen them, and close them again while moving the hand aside (to the dominant side). Hold the hand still briefly.

KING.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape with the dominant hand at the nondominant shoulder, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the hand diagonally downward to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape with the dominant hand on the dominant side of the abdomen (the lower part of the trunk, just above the waist).

SEE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape with the middle finger touching the dominant side of the nose, index finger pointing up. Move the hand forward while rotating it so the index finger points forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape several inches in front of the face, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing up.

THE-TWO-OF-US.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape within a few inches of the chest, in between the signer's chest and that of the other referent, the index finger pointing to chest of the other referent, palm up. Rock the hand back and forth so that the middle finger points back to the signer.

THE-TWO-OF-YOU.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, the index finger pointing to chest of one referent, palm facing across. Rock the hand repeatedly back and forth between the previous and next posture by nodding the wrist. Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the chest, middle finger pointing to the other referent, palm facing across. Hold the hand still briefly.

CUTE.t: One-handed, with a smile expressing cuteness or admiration of something cute: Posture the dominant hand in the "H" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up. Repeatedly flatten and extend the middle and index finger. Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back and extended fingers pointing up.

BOY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "flat C" handshape at the forehead. Repeatedly flatten and open the hand to alternate between the previous and next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape at the forehead. Hold the hand still briefly.

I-FORMAL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing up, extended finger(s) pointing back. Move the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing up, extended finger(s) pointing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

PRO-FORMAL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing up, extended finger(s) pointing back. Move the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing up, extended finger(s) pointing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

PRO-FORMAL-PL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing up, extended finger(s) pointing back. Move the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape on the trunk, dominant palm facing up, extended finger(s) pointing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

YOU-FORMAL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the finger tips pointing toward the sternum of the referent, dominant palm facing up. Move the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the finger tips pointing toward the trunk of the referent, dominant palm facing up. Hold the hand still briefly.

PRO-FORMAL-1.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the finger tips pointing toward the sternum of the referent, dominant palm facing up. Move the hand down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the finger tips pointing toward the trunk of the referent, dominant palm facing up. Hold the hand still briefly.

A.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Move both hands down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of and beside the trunk. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of and beside the trunk. Hold both hands still briefly.

INDIVIDUAL.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest. Move both hands down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of and beside the trunk. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of and beside the trunk. Hold both hands still briefly.

MOVE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape in front of the center of the chest, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands in parallel to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, dominant palm facing down.

DRINK.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a few inches from the mouth, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand forward. Tip the hand up as if tipping a cup to drink from it. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a few inches from the mouth, tip (opposite end from the wrist) of the dominant hand facing up.

FOOD.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape at the mouth, dominant palm facing back. Optionally tap the fingers to the mouth multiple times. Hold the hand still briefly.

OK.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "O" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Move the hand to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "K" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward.

EAT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape within a few inches from the mouth, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape at the mouth, dominant palm facing back. Move both hands alternatingly forward and back to the mouth. Posture the nondominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape at the mouth, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape within a few inches from the mouth, dominant palm facing back.

SIT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "H" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "H" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand, extended fingers of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally) and palm facing down.

ORANGE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a few inches from the chin. Squeeze the hand repeatedly. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape within a few inches from the chin.

WANT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up. Pull both hands a few inches back toward the body while slightly flexing the fingers. Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape a few inches in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape a few inches in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up.

WHO.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "L" handshape at the chin, thumb of the dominant hand pointing back. Repeatedly retract and extend the index finger. When used interrogatively, this sign is produced furrowed eyebrows, squinted eyes, head tilted, and a very small headshake (i.e. pivoting slightly from side to side, not nearly so much as that of a "no" gesture).

WRITE-DOWN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Open the dominant hand up and bring it down onto the nondominant hand so the palms touch. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down.

MONDAY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "M" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

M.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "M" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

T.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "M" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

W.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "M" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

F.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "M" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

S.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "M" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

SUPPOSE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "I" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand forward to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "I" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back.

IF.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "I" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand forward to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "I" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back.

LUCK.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Turn the hand at the wrist to face outward and slightly to the side of the face.

LUCKY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Turn the hand at the wrist to face outward and slightly to the side of the face.

GOOD-LUCK.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Turn the hand at the wrist to face outward and slightly to the side of the face.

MORNING.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "flat B" handshape in the crook of the dominant arm, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "flat B" handshape with the elbow against the abdomen and the arm straight up, dominant palm facing up. Bring the dominant arm up until the palm is facing back near the shoulder with the nondominant hand still in the crook of the elbow.

CULTURE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand, palm of the dominant hand facing forward and oriented so the whole hand points up. Move the dominant hand in an arc, first toward the dominant side, then forward, then back toward the nondominant side. While doing so, rotate the dominant hand from palm-forward orientation to palm-back. The nondominant hand does not move. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand, palm of the dominant hand facing back and oriented so the whole hand points up. Hold both hands still briefly.

CULTURAL.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand, palm of the dominant hand facing forward and oriented so the whole hand points up. Move the dominant hand in an arc, first toward the dominant side, then forward, then back toward the nondominant side. While doing so, rotate the dominant hand from palm-forward orientation to palm-back. The nondominant hand does not move. Posture the nondominant hand in the "1" handshape in front of the center of the chest, extended finger(s) of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "C" shape within a couple of inches of the extended finger of the nondominant hand, palm of the dominant hand facing back and oriented so the whole hand points up. Hold both hands still briefly.

FEEL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. While maintaining contact with the chest, move the hand up to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing back.

FEELING.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. While maintaining contact with the chest, move the hand up to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing back.

WAIT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the trunk, dominant palm facing up. Wiggle the fingers of both hands repeatedly.

PENDING.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the trunk, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the trunk, dominant palm facing up. Wiggle the fingers of both hands repeatedly.

EASTER.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "E" handshape in front of and beside the neck, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "E" handshape in front of and beside the neck, palm facing across. Twist the wrists so the palms face forward. Posture the nondominant hand in the "E" handshape in front of and beside the neck, palm facing forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "E" handshape in front of and beside the neck, palm facing forward. Hold both hands still briefly.

INFORM.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Flat O" handshape at the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Move the hand in an arc toward toward the directional object by extending the elbow. Posture the dominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape several inches from the dominant side of the forehead, dominant palm facing up.

OBSERVE.t: This two-handed ASL sign has two postures: Form the "V" handshape with the dominant hand near the eyes, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down. Form the "V" handshape with the weak hand near the mouth, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down. Move both hands forward. Form the "V" handshape with the dominant hand a medial distance in front of the eyes, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down. Form the "V" handshape with the weak hand a medial distance in front of the mouth, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down.

OBSERVATION.t: This two-handed ASL sign has two postures: Form the "V" handshape with the dominant hand near the eyes, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down. Form the "V" handshape with the weak hand near the mouth, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down. Move both hands forward. Form the "V" handshape with the dominant hand a medial distance in front of the eyes, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down. Form the "V" handshape with the weak hand a medial distance in front of the mouth, extended fingers pointing forward, palm down.

JOG.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "S" handshape in front of and beside the trunk, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, palm facing across. Move both hands in circles parallel with the midline (moving neither right nor left).

DOUBT.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape between the eyes and tip of the nose, dominant palm facing back. Bend the extended fingers while moving the hand down and forward to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "Bent V" handshape several inches from the chin, dominant palm facing back.

STRESSED-OUT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "X" handshape on the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Separate the hands by moving the dominant hand up and the nondominant hand down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "X" handshape on the abdomen, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing back.

STRESS-OUT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "X" handshape on the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape on the chest, dominant palm facing back. Separate the hands by moving the dominant hand up and the nondominant hand down to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "X" handshape on the abdomen, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape on the sternum, dominant palm facing back.

WILL.t: This one-handed ASL sign has two postures: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape just forward of the shoulder at nose height, fingers pointing up. Move the hand forward to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape about an elbow's length in front of the body, at nose height, fingers slightly forward.

SHAVE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape Cheek, palm facing forward. Make a slight arc movement to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape at the chin, palm facing forward. Repeat the movement to indicate the continuous aspect of the sign.

SATURDAY.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Move the dominant hand in horizontal circles.

SAME-AS.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down. The ulnar side of the hand or the little finger itself should be pointing toward the first object or reference location. Move the dominant hand side-to-side (toward the second object, then back toward the first, then back toward the second). Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down. The radial side of the hand or the thumb itself should be pointing toward the second object or reference location. Hold the dominant hand briefly in this posture.

ONE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Hold the hand briefly in this posture.

CL-1.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Hold the hand briefly in this posture.

CUT.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape in front of the area of your dominant shoulder and move to the nondominant shoulder while changing repeatedly to the H shape and back, the palm facing toward the body

CRAB.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape in front of the area of your dominant shoulder and move to the nondominant shoulder while changing repeatedly to the H shape and back, the palm facing toward the body

FRIEND.t: Two-handed: Posture both hands in the "X" handshape with the index fingers hooked together in front of the center of the chest, dominant palm facing down and nondominant palm facing up. Hold both hands briefly in this posture. Unhook the index fingers and rotate each hand to move to the following posture. Posture both hands in the "X" handshape with the index fingers hooked together in front of the center of the chest, dominant palm facing up and nondominant palm facing down. Hold both hands briefly in this posture.

TIME.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "claw 5" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape with the dominant hand at the back of the nondominant wrist, dominant palm facing down. Tap the index finger of the dominant hand onto the nondominant wrist repeatedly.

RESTAURANT.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "R" handshape on the dominant side of the chin, extended fingers pointing up. Hold the hand briefly still. Move the hand down off the chin. Posture the dominant hand in the "R" handshape below the dominant side of the chin. Move the hand up and across to the next posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "R" handshape on the nondominant side of the chin, extended fingers pointing up. Move the hand down off the chin. Posture the dominant hand in the "R" handshape below the nondominant side of the chin. Hold the hand briefly still.

CELEBRATE.t: Two-handed: Posture both hands in the "X" handshape beside the space in front of the chin. Move both hands in horizontal circles.

SEATTLE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape a few inches in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Hold the hand still briefly. Move the hand a few inches from side to side. Hold the hand still briefly.

RECENTLY.t: One-handed, with the head turned slightly toward the nondominant side and with the dominant cheek tensed: Posture the dominant hand in the "X" handshape with the ulnar side of the index finger against the cheek, palm facing back. Repeatedly flex and loosen the medial joint of the index finger.

EXACT.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "Small O" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "Small O" handshape with the tip of the dominant thumb and index finger near the tip of the nondominant thumb and index finger, dominant palm facing down. Imagine a line running through both thumb tips. The imaginary line should be perpendicular to both palms. Hold both hands still briefly Move the dominant hand so the tip of the thumb and finger encircles the imaginary line one or more times. Drop the dominant hand down along the imaginary line so the tip of the dominant thumb and finger contacts the tip of the nondominant thumb and finger. Hold both hands still briefly

APPROXIMATE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "Small O" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "Small O" handshape with the tip of the dominant thumb and index finger near the tip of the nondominant thumb and index finger, dominant palm facing down. Imagine a line running through both thumb tips. The imaginary line should be perpendicular to both palms. Hold both hands still briefly Move the dominant hand so the tip of the thumb and finger encircles the imaginary line one or more times. Drop the dominant hand down along the imaginary line so the tip of the dominant thumb and finger contacts the tip of the nondominant thumb and finger. Hold both hands still briefly

RIDE-IN.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "C" shape in front of the center of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "Bent V" handshape with the dominant index finger and middle finger wrapped over the nondominant thumb, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands forward.

RIDE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "C" shape in front of the center of the chest. Posture the dominant hand in the "Bent V" handshape with the dominant index finger and middle finger wrapped over the nondominant thumb, dominant palm facing down. Move both hands forward.

UNDERSTAND.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Small O" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Release the index finger from the thumb, extending it fully to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Optionally close the index finger back to the thumb and release it again.

DONT-UNDERSTAND.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Small O" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Release the index finger from the thumb, extending it fully to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape within a few inches of the dominant side of the forehead, near the temple, dominant palm facing back. Optionally close the index finger back to the thumb and release it again.

OLD.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape at the chin. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape several inches from the chin.

AGE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape at the chin. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape several inches from the chin.

REVIEW.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "open R" (Ru) handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally). Rotate the dominant hand forward and down, pivoting on the dominant thumb. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "open R" (Ru) handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally) and extended fingers pointing down.

WRONG.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape at the chin, dominant palm facing back. Hold the hand still briefly.

STAND.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down. Hold both hands still briefly.

JUMP.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down. Bend the index and middle finger of the dominant hand while moving it a few inches up to the following posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "Bent V" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down.

DANCE.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the center of the trunk (typically with the upper arm hanging straight down from the shoulder, the elbow bent at a right angle, and the forearm pointing diagonally ahead from the elbow), nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing down. Move the finger tips of the dominant hand from side to side by rotating the forearm repeatedly.

YES.t: One-handed, often with the head nodding "yes": Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Nod the hand at least once. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing down.

MANY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "S" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up. Release the fingers and extend the thumb while moving the hand slightly up and/or forward. Posture the nondominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing up. ( how many? ): When used interrogatively, it is produced with furrowed eyebrows, squinted eyes, head tilted, and a very small headshake (i.e. pivoting slightly from side to side, not nearly so much as that of a "no" gesture).

THERE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing down. Hold the hand still briefly. The sign may also be produced with different palm orientations, but if the radial (thumb-side) edge of the hand faces up, this sign becomes a homophone for 1@InsideChesthigh-RadialUp ( " you, he, she, it " ) API.

YELLOW.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder. Repeatedly twist the hand clockwise and counterclockwise. Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back.

FIRST.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Supinate the hand by twisting it so the palm faces back. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back.

LAST.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Supinate the hand by twisting it so the palm faces back. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back.

ONE-DOLLAR.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Supinate the hand by twisting it so the palm faces back. Posture the dominant hand in the "1" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back.

DRUG.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape within a couple of inches from the base (elbow end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing up. Move the hand back and forth, toward and away from the base of the forearm. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape at the base (elbow end) of the nondominant forearm, dominant palm facing up. When used as a verb, there is just one movement toward the arm instead of a repeated movement back and forth.

STUCK.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape within a few inches from the top of the neck, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back. Drop finger tips down to the following posture. Posture the dominant hand in the "V" handshape at the bottom of the neck, extended finger(s) of the dominant hand pointing back.

GOODBYE.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "open B" handshape about half an arm's length in front of and beside the chest, palm facing forward. Flap the four fingers up and down as a group to form the "Bent B" handshape repeatedly.

EACH.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture while twisting the hand so the base faces to the side and the thumb points across the body toward the base of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape several inches of the ulnar (little-finger) side of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally).

EVERY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture while twisting the hand so the base faces to the side and the thumb points across the body toward the base of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape several inches of the ulnar (little-finger) side of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally).

ANY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture while twisting the hand so the base faces to the side and the thumb points across the body toward the base of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape several inches of the ulnar (little-finger) side of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally).

MOST.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape within a couple of inches of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing up. Move the dominant hand in an arc to the next posture while twisting the hand so the base faces to the side and the thumb points across the body toward the base of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open A" handshape in front of the center of the chest, thumb of the nondominant hand pointing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "open A" handshape several inches of the ulnar (little-finger) side of the nondominant palm, thumb of the dominant hand pointing across the body toward the nondominant side (contralaterally).

TECHNOLOGY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand in a couple of inches of the ulnar (little-finger-side) edge of the nondominant hand, palm facing across. Tap the middle finger of the dominant hand once or more on the ulnar edge of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the ulnar (little-finger-side) edge of the nondominant hand, palm facing across. Hold both hands still briefly.

TECHNICAL.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand in a couple of inches of the ulnar (little-finger-side) edge of the nondominant hand, palm facing across. Tap the middle finger of the dominant hand once or more on the ulnar edge of the nondominant hand. Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing back. Posture the dominant hand in the "open 8" handshape with the dominant hand at the ulnar (little-finger-side) edge of the nondominant hand, palm facing across. Hold both hands still briefly.

NEW-YORK.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "open B" handshape in front of the center of the chest, nondominant palm facing up. Posture the dominant hand in the "Y" handshape with the dominant hand at the palm of the nondominant hand, dominant palm facing down. Move the dominant hand from side to side across the nondominant hand while holding the nondominant hand still.

TRY.t: Two-handed: Posture the nondominant hand in the "T" handshape a few inches in front of the nondominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Posture the dominant hand in the "T" handshape a few inches in front of the dominant side of the chest, palm facing across. Pronate the hands while moving them forward to the next posture. Posture the nondominant hand in the "T" handshape about half arm's length in front of the nondominant side of the chest, nondominant palm facing down. Posture the dominant hand in the "T" handshape about half arm's length in front of the dominant side of the chest, dominant palm facing down.

FATHER.t: This one-handed ASL sign has one repeated posture: Posture the dominant hand in the "5" handshape with the thumb touching the forehead. Repeatedly touch the thumb to the forehead.

ASL.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "A" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "S" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Posture the dominant hand in the "L" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward.

I-LOVE-YOU.t: One-handed, with an affectionate smile: Posture the dominant hand in the "I/L/Y" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing forward. Hold the hand briefly in this posture. The hand may be moved or rotated to indicate the subject and object of the affection. The back of the hand faces toward the subject. The palm faces toward the object.

0.t: Posture the dominant hand in the "O" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, palm facing across.

FOUR.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Hold the hand briefly in this posture.

FJ.t: One-handed: Posture the dominant hand in the "4" handshape about half an arm's length in front of the shoulder, dominant palm facing back. Hold the hand briefly in this posture.
